To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) transformation of mutant strains of P. pneumoniae which lack the enzyme α-amylomaltase, with DNA from a donor strain which can produce this enzyme, results in its rapid formation; (2) the rate of formation is proportional to the amount of permanent genetic change elicited by the DNA in the recipient cells; (3) the enzyme is produced at its maximal level, as a constant proportion of newly-synthesized protein, within about 10 minutes after DNA uptake;

the formation of amylase in pneumococci transformed with donor DNA occurs within 10 minutes after transformation, that the rate of enzyme formation is proportional to the amount of DNA incorporated, and that the rate is proportional to the degree of recombination.

(1) the transformation of a mutant strain of Streptococcus mutans with DNA from a strain that is wild-type at the amylomalt gene results in the rapid production of amylom altase, (2) the rate of production of the enzyme is proportional to the rate of genetic change, and (3) the production of amylomal tase requires the interaction of donor DNA with host DNA, presumably by recombination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of genetic transformation.
the mechanism of the process of transformation.
the mechanism of genetic transformation of bacteria, and in particular, the mechanism by which DNA is integrated into the host cell.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the DNA is integrated into the cell and is then replicated and recombined with the host chromosome, and that this process occurs in the first few minutes of transformation.
transformation involves all the events that are necessary to produce the new phenotype, and that these events occur in a very short time.
the process of transformation of pneumococci is a rapid and efficient one, which involves the integration and recombination of DNA and the elicitation of specific enzyme synthesis.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transformation of pneumococci with DNA from another pneumococcus, results in a rapid, specific synthesis of a new protein, amylomaltage.
the process of transformation is a rapid and complex one, and that the genetic information in the DNA must be in an active and highly ordered state.

the genetic transformation of pneumo- cocci involves a series of steps, which are: (1) uptake of DNA by the recipient cell; (2) interaction of donor and host DNA to produce recombinants; (3) integration of donor DNA into host DNA; (4) replication of donor DNA; and (5) elicitation of specific enzyme formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA that is introduced into cells is able to be expressed very rapidly.
transformation of mutant strains with DNA from a donor strain which can produce an enzyme results in the rapid synthesis of that enzyme.
DNA must not just enter the cell, but must be integrated in the cell and replicated in order to elict enzyme synthesis.
